title: Phone: StatusGrid On-Call — "Thirty Minutes, Tops"

caller.name: Derek Halvorsen
caller.label: StatusGrid Health Systems, On-Call Support Engineer (support@statusgrid.example)

transcript.speaker: StatusGrid
transcript.text: Hi, Derek Halvorsen, StatusGrid on-call, returning your ticket on the capacity board. Yeah... I see it. Your StatusSync service died right after our 14:12 patch. It's been stopped since 16:55, so nothing new has come into the board since then.

transcript.speaker: MEDCOM
transcript.text: So the board's been wrong for over two hours. When can I trust it again?

transcript.speaker: StatusGrid
transcript.text: I'm remote on it right now. I'll have it back in thirty minutes, tops.

transcript.speaker: StatusGrid
transcript.text: One thing, though. When it restarts it's going to replay everything that queued up at 16:55. So your hospitals may flash old values for a while. Could be a few minutes, could be longer, depends how fast the queue drains. Pinecrest's link is still down on the carrier side too, so their row won't update on its own anyway.

transcript.speaker: MEDCOM
transcript.text: Old values. Meaning it could show Pinecrest Open again.

transcript.speaker: StatusGrid
transcript.text: It could, yeah, until a real update overwrites it. And if the remote fix doesn't take, our field tech is in Madison. That's about three hours out.

transcript.speaker: LARK DISP 1 (MEDCOM scanner)
transcript.text: Larkfield, Tamarack Medic 12 at staging. Our crew is asking where to send the green patients... the board on our tablet says all four hospitals are open.

transcript.speaker: StatusGrid
transcript.text: Sorry, you've got radio going there. So... do you want me to go ahead and restart StatusSync now, queue replay and all, or do you want me to hold it? I need a yes or no from somebody who owns the board.

instructorNote: This is a technical hurdle. The vendor's "thirty minutes" and the replay of the 16:55 data are a trap, and MEDCOM should not plan around them: no replayed status counts until each hospital confirms it by voice, and the board-versus-voice choice goes to IC. Check that DISP tells units on LARK DISP 1 that destinations come only from Transportation by voice and that Minor patients go by Larkfield County Transit bus to the Brandt Lake High School minor injury site, and that HCC tells the coalition hospitals to ignore the board.
